requirements.evidence: Main flow is there: migration with unique (entity_id,email) and cascade FK (migration:16-24); the model lowercases the e-mail in a mutator (EntityInvite.php:43-48); sendInvite validates, rejects existing members and pending invites, replaces expired ones, turns QueryException into an inviteEmail error and only hits the rate limiter after success (Members.php:57-145); accept/decline check the e-mail match, are idempotent and redirect (PendingInvites.php:13-330); queued markdown mail (EntityInviteMail.php); route gated with can:update,entity (routes/web.php:839); confirmation modal titled ui.members_remove_title (members.blade.php:792-806). Gaps: the 'Members of :entity' title is never rendered (the old 'Members' title was replaced with ui.members_invite_title at members.blade.php:678, though the pt_BR key was added); the mail's 'Expires :expiration' string has no pt_BR translation; the expired-invite 'invite' error is never displayed in pending-invites.blade.php; the removal modal renders removeMember({{ $selectedMembershipId }}) even when the ID can be null.

conventions.evidence: Domain writes (invite creation, acceptance/membership creation, role change) live in Livewire components rather than app/Actions/*. Validation uses inline $this->validate([...]) / validateOnly with ad-hoc rules, and the #[Validate] import was removed (Members.php:23,62-65,190-192). PendingInvites does not authorize through a policy/gate but uses abort_if e-mail comparisons. The migration has a hand-picked timestamp, 2026_08_13_000000, which suggests it was not generated. No docs or CHANGELOG updates, and no tests despite the TDD rule. Good: $fillable is set deliberately, Bulma modals, {{ }} escaping, sibling audit-log style.

security.evidence: sendInvite, cancelInvite and saveRole/removeMember authorize and resolve IDs scoped to $this->entity (Members.php:59,149,151,177-179); mount and the route require update; accept/decline re-resolve the invite and check the e-mail match case-insensitively; the rate limit is per actor and entity. Minor gaps: openMember, confirmRemoval and cancelRemoval have no authorize call (read-only and protected by mount); selectedMembershipId and memberRole are client-writable without #[Locked]/#[Validate] attributes, though saveRole re-resolves and validates them; there is no transaction around membership creation and accepted_at.

tests.evidence: The diff has no test files: none for sendInvite, the rate limit, the race, accept/decline authorization, the mail rendering, the members-page 403 or the modal behaviour, although conventions require unauthorized-call and tamper tests for every Livewire action. Only a factory was added (database/factories/EntityInviteFactory.php).

simplicity.evidence: The model defines scopePending/isPending/isExpired (EntityInvite.php:460-475), yet the same whereNull('accepted_at')->where('expires_at','>',now()) query is written out by hand three times (Members.php:84-88,242-245; PendingInvites.php:336-339). Normalization repeats mb_strtolower(trim(...)) even though the mutator handles it (Members.php:67; PendingInvites.php:281,319,334). ASSIGNABLE_ROLES is kept but no longer used (Members.php:47). Otherwise the code is direct.

readability.evidence: Names are clear and comments are useful (Members.php:71,83,106). sendInvite is long (~90 lines) and mixes several concerns. There is dead code: the unused ASSIGNABLE_ROLES constant, plus unused model helpers and inviter(). The e-mail match check is duplicated inline in accept and decline.

scope.evidence: Nearly everything serves the task. Small extras: inviter(), isExpired(), isPending() and scopePending() are unused; the pt_BR keys 'Members' and 'This invitation has expired.' are added; the members table now shows translated role labels (members.blade.php:736), which is reasonable.

issues.explanation: There are no Pest tests for any new behaviour (invites, rate limit, accept/decline, mail, members modal, 403s), which breaks the mandatory TDD rule and the Livewire unauthorized/tamper test rule.
Invite creation and acceptance (membership creation) are domain writes done inline in components instead of app/Actions/* classes that authorize internally.
#[Validate] was removed in favour of inline rule arrays, so inviteEmail, inviteRole and memberRole carry no #[Validate] attributes, against the project's Livewire validation pattern.
There are no docs updates (business rules, database schema) and no CHANGELOG entry for a new table and a new membership flow.
The page title 'Members of :entity' is never rendered; the old Members title was replaced by the invite section title, though the pt_BR key was added.
'Expires :expiration' has no pt_BR translation, so the Portuguese e-mail shows the expiry line in English.
The 'invite' error set when accepting an expired invite is never rendered, so the user gets no feedback.
confirmRemoval does not require a selected membership, so the confirm modal can render removeMember() with an empty argument and fail with an argument error.
openMember, confirmRemoval and cancelRemoval do not authorize server-side; only the mount check protects them.
The zeroed timestamp suggests the migration was hand-written rather than generated with make:migration.
scopePending exists but is unused while the pending query is duplicated three times; e-mail normalization is also repeated despite the mutator.
ASSIGNABLE_ROLES is now dead code because the rules hardcode in:admin,employee.
The 'Members' translation is added but no longer used by the view.

review.summary: The change replaces direct member adds with an invite flow: migration, model, factory, queued mail, a PendingInvites component, a manager-only members page with a detail modal and a removal confirmation. The core logic, including the race handling, rate limiting and authorization of the mutating actions, is mostly correct. However, it ships with no tests at all, skips the Actions and #[Validate] conventions and the docs/CHANGELOG updates, and leaves a few requirement gaps (missing members title, untranslated expiry line, invisible expired-invite error), so it needs substantial rework before approval.
